decisions.reason: A classic lever handle close to the core range costs little to carry, and in a growing market with ample slack there is no performance shortfall that would trigger search for other uses of its resources.
A lever handle family extends the firm's system breadth at low marginal cost, and one year is too early to judge it below aspiration.
A single new handle design fits the established design-led portfolio, and the firm's slack lets it be carried while its market results remain uncertain.
Like C, it is a low-risk design addition close to the core business, and nothing indicates a shortfall that would justify withdrawing it within a year.
A handle family supports the strategy of integrated system families, and a young product in a growing industry is unlikely to be dropped this soon.

The L700 electronic access system, promoted for its market-unique light technology, is central to the firm's push into digital building organization, so it is strategically important and will be supported.
